entries.claim: The registry task limits itself to four rows even though CEN-01 requires every hand-maintained census in the repository to be registered.
entries.failure_scenario: The plan itself identifies existing hand-maintained counts in `lib/bulk-output.mjs`, `lib/text-transport.mjs`, `lib/rung-agent.mjs`, `lib/deferred-reads.mjs`, and `planning-lease-check.test.mjs` as remaining outside the registry. None receives a marker or registry row. Edits that invalidate any of those counts will therefore never be identified by the plan-time check, and their unregistered sites will not fail the suite, violating CEN-01 and Success Criterion 1's stated completeness.

entries.claim: The registry immutability verification does not prove the required deeply frozen table: it checks the outer table and subject lists, but not entry objects.
entries.failure_scenario: An implementation can `Object.freeze` the exported array and each `subjects` array while leaving entries mutable. Both Task 1 one-liners (push and subject-list mutation) and Task 4's stated assertions pass, yet a consumer can change `REGISTRY[0].holdingFile`, `id`, `what`, or `assertingSite` at runtime. That violates Task 1's required deeply frozen registry and permits the imported plan-time predicate to be silently corrupted.

entries.claim: The `/cad-plan` wiring task has no falsifiable verification that the gate runs before dispatch, halts on refusal, or covers the inline path.
entries.failure_scenario: Task 6 verifies only that `plan-time` appears once in `plan.md` and that self-verify accepts the invocation. A workflow can contain that one command after an executor dispatch, describe it as non-blocking, or omit the effective inline-path pointer while satisfying both checks. The phase would then pass its listed verification even though CEN-02 and Success Criterion 4's central guarantee-refuse after PLAN creation and before any executor on both paths-fails.
